questions.question: Describe the full recipe for building the general term of a linear pattern, and the verification step that protects it.
questions.expected_answer: Check every gap gives the same constant difference d (term after minus term before). Write Tn = dn + c where the correction c = T1 − d, because dn has already taken one step of size d at position one. Verify by substituting a known position (especially n = 1) and confirming the formula reproduces that term.

questions.question: Explain the three question types powered by a general term — forwards, backwards, and membership — using Tn = 3n + 2 as the example.
questions.expected_answer: Forwards: substitute a position, T50 = 3(50) + 2 = 152. Backwards: set Tn equal to a value and solve, 3n + 2 = 92 gives n = 30, so 92 is the 30th term. Membership: solve the same way and judge n — 3n + 2 = 100 gives n = 98/3, not a natural number, proving 100 is not a term.

questions.question: In story or picture problems (matchsticks, tables, tariffs), what do d and the correction represent physically, and what is the classic counting trap?
questions.expected_answer: d is what each new step genuinely adds (3 matches per new square, the per-kilometre rate); the correction is the fixed part (the extra match of the first square, the flat call-out fee). The trap is shared parts — a shared matchstick wall or swallowed seats — so count at least three figures and check the formula reproduces figure one.
